explanation: Both predict action sequences to manage the control horizon, but CVAE chunking and diffusion are different policy distributions, not successive checkpoints.
Octo describes itself as a transformer-based diffusion policy scaled through diverse robot pretraining.
RT-2 succeeds RT-1 in the same research line but changes to a pretrained VLM and text-form actions; this is not RT-1 weight continuation.
RT-1-X applies the RT-1 architecture to cross-embodiment data.
RT-2-X is the VLM-based RT-X instantiation.
Octo pretraining uses the Open X-Embodiment dataset; RT-X weights are not the Octo backbone.
OpenVLA uses the Open X-Embodiment data ecosystem while choosing its own VLM architecture.
Both map VLM features to discretized autoregressive actions; similarity is architectural, not proof of inherited private RT-2 weights.
OFT modifies OpenVLA fine-tuning and action decoding while retaining its pretrained foundation.
pi0-FAST uses FAST tokenization to instantiate an autoregressive variant; FAST itself is a representation method.
pi0.5 builds on pi0 and adds heterogeneous training and hierarchical task behavior.
Knowledge insulation uses FAST action tokens as an auxiliary learning signal for the VLM backbone.
The pi0.6 model card explicitly builds on pi0.5 while changing backbone, action expert and data.
RECAP trains pi0.6 with offline and on-robot RL, yielding pi-star-0.6.
The memory experiments augment pi0.6 with visual and language memory.
pi0.7 retains the pi0.6 architectural foundation and changes context conditioning.
pi0.7 uses the MEM-style visual-history encoder and memory system.
pi0.7 uses experience from RL-trained specialists with strategy metadata to absorb their behaviors.
Both couple VLM features to flow action generation, but GR00T uses cross-attention and embodiment adapters; they do not share published checkpoints.
The GR00T N1 paper explicitly cites ACT for action chunking.
N1.5 modifies the VLM, data and future-feature objective relative to N1.
N1.6 replaces/updates the backbone, enlarges the DiT and changes action representations.
The repository positions N1.7 as the next N1 release, with a new Cosmos-Reason2 backbone and deployment support.
The 1.5 report extends the Gemini Robotics line through motion transfer and reasoning/action interleaving.
Robotics 2 extends the earlier upper-body focus into whole-body control.
ER 1.6 follows ER 1.5 within the reasoning branch; it does not replace the VLA action decoder.
ER 2 is the later embodied reasoning model in the same family, now based on Gemini 3.5 Flash.
ER 2 supplies planning and coordination while Robotics 2 produces executable robot behavior.
The On-Device 2 model card explicitly names Robotics 1.5 technology and on-device Gemma as its basis.
RDT scales continuous generative action modeling and adds unified physical action semantics; comparison is methodological, not weight inheritance.
OpenDriveLab UniVLA explicitly acknowledges OpenVLA code; its defining change is learning task-centric latent actions from video.
Two independently authored UniVLA papers have different arXiv IDs, repositories, architectures and objectives.
Both need canonical physical action mappings across embodiments; no direct RDT checkpoint inheritance is claimed.
Soft prompts and embodiment adapters are alternative ways to separate shared representations from hardware-specific interfaces.
RTC is introduced for action-chunking flow policies and addresses latency without replacing semantic pretraining.
N1.6 reports using real-time chunking during asynchronous robot rollouts.
